title: Tries
objective: Store words one letter per node, so prefix searches take as many steps as the prefix has letters.

sources.title: Sedgewick and Wayne, Algorithms, 4th ed.: section 5.2, Tries

simplifies: Each node here stores its children in a dict. Real tries also store a value per word (like a count) and can be compressed by merging chains of single children.

quiz.prompt: A trie holds 10,000 words. How many steps does starts_with("ca") take?

options.explanation: Right. One step per letter of the prefix, however many words are stored.
That is checking every word. The trie only follows the letters.
It doesn't depend on the number of words at all; only on the prefix length.

quiz.prompt: Why mark the end of each word?

options.text: So "car" is known to be a word, not just the start of "cart"
options.explanation: Right. Without the mark, a prefix and a whole word look the same.
It adds a little information; it doesn't save space.
Order isn't the reason; telling words from prefixes is.
